item.title: Iran expert says Trump's 'war of choice' has morphed into a 'war of necessity'
item.summary: With the Strait of Hormuz blocked, policy expert Karim Sadjadpour says the war in Iran is becoming increasingly complicated: "I don't think President Trump ... understood what he was getting into."

item.title: USS Ford has seen war, fire and plumbing woes as it nears a record long deployment
item.summary: The Ford's crew left Norfolk, Va., on June 24, initially bound for the Mediterranean. More than nine months later, the crew is now in the Red Sea for the war with Iran with no clear return date.

item.title: Ukraine strings nets over cities as killer drones turn streets into war zones
item.summary: In eastern Ukraine, white nylon nets now stretch over roads and city streets, a low-tech defense against deadly FPV drones that dominate the battlefield and threaten civilians near the front line.

item.title: Khamenei's killing renews questions about U.S. assassinating foreign leaders
item.summary: Technology allowed the U.S. and Israel to kill Iran's Supreme Leader, but raised longstanding questions about whether the U.S. as a democracy should be assassinating foreign leaders.

item.title: Daniel Biss wins Democratic primary for closely-watched Illinois House seat
item.summary: Biss, the mayor of Evanston, Ill., topped political newcomer Kat Abughazaleh, a first-time candidate who ran as an unapologetic progressive in the race to succeed longtime incumbent Jan Schakowsky.

item.title: Arizona AG files criminal charges against Kalshi over 'illegal gambling'
item.summary: Arizona is the first state to allege the prediction market company has committed criminal violations, accusing it of running an unlicensed gambling operation.

item.title: Judge orders 1,000 Voice of America staffers back to work in rebuke to Kari Lake
item.summary: A federal judge has ordered more than a thousand Voice of America staffers back to work by Monday. It's a major defeat for the Trump administration's effort to cut the news outlet to the bones.

item.title: Adam Gopnik salutes the immigrant experience that shaped American music
item.summary: In a conversation with pianist Lara Downes, the New Yorker staff writer says music in America will keep evolving as long as the country keeps an open door to new people and new sounds.

item.title: Sparse evidence for cannabis to treat mental health conditions highlights research gap
item.summary: A new analysis represents the largest effort yet to systematically parse all the data from high-quality clinical trials on cannabis and mental health. The evidence is lacking.

item.title: She's won 24 Paralympic medals. But Oksana Masters wants to talk about times she lost
item.summary: Oksana Masters leaves Italy with five new para Nordic skiing medals, extending her reign as the most decorated U.S. Winter Paralympian. She competes in summer sports too and is already eyeing LA 2028.
